text: The ovens just went on humming low and steady in the shop, air thick with yeast and burnt sugar. Elias wiped flour off his arms, glanced at the clock, 3:17 AM, Thursday. He walked up to the front counter. There was a book sitting on the glass display case, this worn paperback called *The Shadow of the Wind*. Had been there six weeks now, just sitting. Normally he would grab it and put it in the return bin behind the register, assume a mixed up customer dropped it there by mistake. But tonight it felt different. The book was warm, slightly warmer than the cold air of the shop. He opened it to a marked page, and this folded square of lined notebook paper slipped out and landed on the counter. Elias stopped for a second then opened it up. Writing was jagged and hurried. *I know you’re reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything.* His heart went crazy, banging on his ribs, a sharp odd beat cutting through the quiet mixer noise. He looked around the shop. Empty. Shadows long on the tiles. Nobody there. He looked at the note, looked at the book. Hands shaking a bit, went to page 204. Words got blurry in front of his face. He closed the book, slammed it flat on the counter, and went to get his pen.
